subject: [hw] DEC07 -> hw-lead: include/redwood_vcodec.h rev 3 text (RWVC_WIN_VDEC_ALL); DEC04/DEC07/T02 need it landed
body:
hw-lead: here is the exact ABI rev 3 text for include/redwood_vcodec.h, as a patch that applies to the current file (sha256 d824d4b6...38e9034b). DEC07 and DEC04 both need it; T02's fake and T04's t_v40 tables also grow by one entry.

  gpu/hwcodec/kern/test_dec07/patches/redwood_vcodec-rev3.patch

--- a/include/redwood_vcodec.h
+++ b/include/redwood_vcodec.h
@@ -14,6 +14,21 @@
  *   VENC 0x17020000+0x2000, VENC_C1 0x17820000+0x2000, VDEC_SYS 0x1602f000, VDEC_BASE 0x16000000, VDEC_VLD 0x16020000,
  *   VDEC_MC 0x16021000, VDEC_MV 0x16023000, VDEC_MISC 0x16025000+0x4000, VDEC_LAT_MISC 0x16010000, VDEC_LAT_VLD 0x16011000+0x400,
  *   VDEC_RACING 0x16004000, VDEC_SOC_GCON 0x1600f000 (0x1000 each unless given)
+ *   VDEC_ALL 0x16000000+0x30000 (rev 3, 2026-11-11, DEC07; RWVC_WIN_COUNT becomes 13, RWVC_ABI_VERSION stays 1 because
+ *   no existing ioctl or struct changed): the vendor decoder maps 0x16000000+0x40000 and addresses
+ *   sub-blocks that the ten windows above do not cover (facts/VDEC_PROTOCOL.md section 4). This one window spans the
+ *   part it uses up to VDEC_SYS; the power block is decided per 4 KiB page, not per window:
+ *     0x00000-0x0cfff + 0x0e000-0x0efff + 0x20000-0x2ffff -> VDEC_CORE (VDE2): VDEC_BASE 0x16000000 (+0x800 UFO),
+ *       the vendor's 0x16001000/0x16002000/0x16003800, VDEC_RACING 0x16004000, VDEC_VLD 0x16020000, VDEC_MC 0x16021000,
+ *       AVC_VLD 0x16022000, VDEC_MV 0x16023000, PP 0x16024000, VDEC_MISC 0x16025000, 0x16029000, VDEC_SYS 0x1602f000,
+ *       larb4 0x1602e000.
+ *     0x0d000 + 0x0f000-0x1ffff -> VDEC_SOC (VDE): larb5 0x1600d000 (page 0x0d), VDEC_SOC_GCON 0x1600f000,
+ *       VDEC_LAT_MISC 0x16010000, VDEC_LAT_VLD 0x16011000, the vendor's LAT sub-blocks 0x16011800-0x16018800.
+ *   VDEC_CORE takes a hidden reference on VDEC_SOC, so a core page is usable only while both domains are on (the core
+ *   clock path needs MT_CG_SOC and MT_CG_VDEC0). The larb pages 0x0d000 (larb5) and 0x2e000 (larb4) are READ-ONLY
+ *   through this window except the words in the kernel's allow-list: larb5 offset 0x00c bit 0, the sleep-protect bit the
+ *   vendor's vdec_hal_wait_larb_sleep_protect sets (opus-dec1's host frame trace). The kernel owns the rest of the larb
+ *   configuration; DEC02's facts/vdec_trace/PAGES.md can add a word (larb4 0x1602e000 has none yet).
  * Power blocks (clk-mt6885-pg.c): VEN 0x344 bit 17 (larb7 0x17010000, vencsys 0x17000000), VEN_CORE1 0x348 bit 18 (larb8
  * 0x17810000, 0x17800000), VDE 0x33c bit 15 (larb5 0x1600d000, vdec_soc_gcon), VDE2 0x340 bit 16 (larb4 0x1602e000, vdec_gcon).
  * Interrupts: VENC SPI 308, VENC_C1 SPI 313?, VDEC core SPI 424, VDEC LAT SPI 425 (K02 verifies; polled mode first).
@@ -25,7 +40,7 @@
 #define RWVC_ABI_VERSION 1u
 enum { RWVC_WIN_VENC = 0, RWVC_WIN_VENC_C1, RWVC_WIN_VDEC_SYS, RWVC_WIN_VDEC_BASE, RWVC_WIN_VDEC_VLD, RWVC_WIN_VDEC_MC,
 	RWVC_WIN_VDEC_MV, RWVC_WIN_VDEC_MISC, RWVC_WIN_VDEC_LAT_MISC, RWVC_WIN_VDEC_LAT_VLD, RWVC_WIN_VDEC_RACING,
-	RWVC_WIN_VDEC_SOC_GCON, RWVC_WIN_COUNT };
+	RWVC_WIN_VDEC_SOC_GCON, RWVC_WIN_VDEC_ALL, RWVC_WIN_COUNT };
 enum { RWVC_BLK_VENC = 0, RWVC_BLK_VENC_C1 = 1, RWVC_BLK_VDEC_SOC = 2, RWVC_BLK_VDEC_CORE = 3, RWVC_BLK_COUNT };
 enum { RWVC_IRQ_VENC = 0, RWVC_IRQ_VENC_C1 = 1, RWVC_IRQ_VDEC = 2, RWVC_IRQ_VDEC_LAT = 3, RWVC_IRQ_COUNT };

Decisions baked in (say if you want them changed):
- RWVC_ABI_VERSION stays 1: an added enum value with no struct/ioctl change cannot break a compiled client; bump only if you want a handshake.
- The map is not the literal "0x00000-0x1ffff VDE" of the first proposal: VDEC_BASE (0x16000000) and VDEC_RACING (0x16004000) are core registers and are already VDEC_CORE in K02's accepted windows; page 0x0e is larb6 (VDE2 clock domain). Mapping them to CORE is stricter (CORE implies SOC) and cannot widen anything. 0x0f000-0x1ffff stays SOC as proposed.
- One larb write is allowed: larb5 0x00c bit 0. opus-dec1's frame trace has the vendor writing bit 0 and polling bit 16 there; a flat read-only rule would hang the first frame (DEC04's finding).

Consequence of RWVC_WIN_COUNT=13 that owners must handle with the header change (I cannot edit their files):
- tests/hw/t_fake.c: EXPECT_BYTES/EXPECT_BLOCK need the 13th entry (0x30000, VDEC_BLK_VDEC_CORE) or T02's loop fails. Patch in gpu/hwcodec/kern/test_dec07/patches/t_fake-vdec-all.patch (sent to hw-t02).
- vcu/test_v40/t_v40.c: fhw_win[RWVC_WIN_COUNT] gains a zero entry; DEC04 owns that.
- tests/phone/rwvc_probe.c: win_name[RWVC_WIN_COUNT] gains a NULL; the phone probe owner must add "VDEC_ALL".
- hwlog/n2vc_hw_log.c: WIN_NAMES[RWVC_WIN_COUNT] likewise.

DEC07's kernel patch and T02's fake patch apply and are tested against this exact header text (and the kernel patch also against rev 2 via a temporary scaffold): N2TEST DEC07 PASS 2370001/2370001, K02 588891/588891 on both header revisions, staged kernel compile 0 unknown symbols. If hw-lead is away, please have opus-kern or root land this header first: it blocks DEC04 and DEC07 and the fake patch. Post the new sha and I re-run.
